sentences.zh: 韓愈，字退之，昌黎人。

translations.literal: Han Yu, styled Tuizhi, was a native of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Han Yu, whose courtesy name was Tuizhi, was a native of Changli.

sentences.zh: 父仲卿，無名位。

translations.literal: His father Zhongqing held no fame or office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhongqing held no fame or office.

sentences.zh: 愈生三歲而孤，養於從父兄。

translations.literal: Yu lost his father at three and was raised by an elder cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was orphaned at the age of three and was raised by an elder cousin.

sentences.zh: 愈自以孤子，幼刻苦學儒，不俟獎勵。

translations.literal: Yu, as an orphan, from youth studied Confucian learning with bitter diligence, without waiting for encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: As an orphan, Yu from childhood applied himself strenuously to Confucian learning, needing no encouragement.

sentences.zh: 大歷、貞元之間，文字多尚古學，效楊雄、董仲舒之述作，而獨孤及、梁肅最稱淵奧，儒林推重。

translations.literal: Between the Dali and Zhenyuan reigns, writing mostly prized antiquarian learning, imitating the compositions of Yang Xiong and Dong Zhongshu; Dugu Ji and Liang Su were most praised for profundity, and the Confucian school held them in esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Dali and Zhenyuan reigns, writers largely favored antiquarian learning and imitated the works of Yang Xiong and Dong Zhongshu. Dugu Ji and Liang Su were most praised for depth, and the scholarly world held them in high regard.

sentences.zh: 愈從其徒遊，銳意鉆仰，欲自振於一代。

translations.literal: Yu traveled with their followers, keenly drilling and looking upward, wishing to raise himself in a generation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu studied under their followers, drilling himself relentlessly in the hope of distinguishing himself in his generation.

sentences.zh: 洎舉進士，投文於公卿間，故相鄭餘慶頗為之延譽，由是知名於時。

translations.literal: When he took the jinshi examination, he submitted writings among ministers and grandees; the former chancellor Zheng Yuqing greatly extended his reputation for him, and by this he became known in his time.
translations.idiomatic: When he sat for the jinshi examination, he circulated his writings among high officials. The former chancellor Zheng Yuqing spoke highly of him, and he thereby became known in his day.

sentences.zh: 尋登進士第。

translations.literal: Soon he passed the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: He soon passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 宰相董晉出鎮大梁，辟為巡官。

translations.literal: When Chancellor Dong Jin went out to command Daliang, he recruited Yu as touring officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Chancellor Dong Jin took up command at Daliang, he recruited Yu as a touring officer.

sentences.zh: 府除，徐州張建封又請為其賓佐。

translations.literal: When the prefecture post ended, Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou also invited him as his aide.
translations.idiomatic: When that appointment ended, Zhang Jianfeng of Xuzhou also invited him to serve as his aide.

sentences.zh: 愈發言真率，無所畏避，操行堅正，拙於世務。

translations.literal: Yu spoke frankly and without fear or avoidance; his conduct was firm and upright, and he was clumsy in worldly affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Yu spoke with blunt sincerity and without fear or evasion. His conduct was firm and upright, but he was awkward in worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 調授四門博士，轉監察御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Four Gates Erudite, then promoted to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Four Gates Erudite and later promoted to Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 德宗晚年，政出多門，宰相不專機務。

translations.literal: In Dezong's later years, government issued from many hands, and the chancellor did not monopolize affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the late years of Emperor Dezong, government issued from many hands, and the chancellor did not monopolize state affairs.

sentences.zh: 宮市之弊，諫官論之不聽。

translations.literal: The abuses of the palace market—remonstrating officials argued against them, but were not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: As for the abuses of the palace market, remonstrating officials spoke against them but were not heeded.

sentences.zh: 愈嘗上章數千言極論之，不聽，怒貶為連州山陽令，量移江陵府掾曹。

translations.literal: Yu once submitted a memorial of several thousand characters strongly arguing the point; it was not heeded, and in anger he was demoted to magistrate of Shanyang in Lianzhou, then transferred in rank to staff officer of Jiangling Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yu once submitted a memorial of several thousand characters arguing the matter at length. It went unheeded, and in anger he was demoted to magistrate of Shanyang in Lianzhou, then transferred in rank to a staff officer of Jiangling Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元和初，召為國子博士，遷都官員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe reign, he was summoned as Erudite of the Directorate of Education, then promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe reign, he was summoned to serve as Erudite of the Directorate of Education and was later promoted to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時華州刺史閻濟美以公事停華陰令柳澗縣務，俾攝掾曹。

translations.literal: At that time Hua Prefecture governor Yan Jimei, on official business, suspended Hua Prefecture magistrate Liu Jian from county duties and had him act as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yan Jimei, governor of Hua Prefecture, suspended the magistrate of Huayin, Liu Jian, from county duties on official grounds and had him serve as acting staff officer.

sentences.zh: 居數月，濟美罷郡，出居公館，澗遂諷百姓遮道索前年軍頓役直。

translations.literal: After several months Yan Jimei left the prefecture and lodged at the official residence; Jian then incited the people to block the road and demand the previous year's military supply labor payments.
translations.idiomatic: After several months Yan Jimei left the prefecture and took lodging at the official residence. Jian then incited the people to block the road and demand payment for the previous year's military supply labor.

sentences.zh: 後刺史趙昌按得澗罪以聞，貶房州司馬。

translations.literal: Later Prefect Zhao Chang investigated and found Jian's crime and reported it; Jian was demoted to prefectural adjutant of Fangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later Prefect Zhao Chang investigated, found Jian guilty, and reported the matter. Jian was demoted to prefectural adjutant of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 愈因使過華，知其事，以為刺史相黨，上疏理澗，留中不下。

translations.literal: Yu, on a mission passing through Hua, learned of the affair and thought the prefect and magistrate were in collusion; he submitted a memorial defending Jian, which was retained in the palace and not issued.
translations.idiomatic: While on a mission passing through Hua, Yu learned of the affair and believed the prefect and magistrate were in collusion. He submitted a memorial defending Jian, but it was retained in the palace and never issued.

sentences.zh: 詔監察御史李宗奭按驗，得澗贓狀，再貶澗封溪尉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Supervising Censor Li Zongshi to investigate and verify; Jian's corrupt conduct was found, and Jian was demoted again to assistant magistrate of Fengxi.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Supervising Censor Li Zongshi to investigate. Jian's corrupt conduct was established, and he was demoted again to assistant magistrate of Fengxi.

sentences.zh: 以愈妄論，復為國子博士。

translations.literal: Because Yu had argued rashly, he was again made Erudite of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yu had argued rashly, he was returned to his post as Erudite of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 愈自以才高，累被擯黜，作《進學解》以自喻曰：

translations.literal: Yu, considering himself highly talented and repeatedly rejected and demoted, composed 'An Explication for Advancing in Learning' to explain himself, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Considering himself highly talented yet repeatedly rejected and demoted, Yu composed An Explication for Advancing in Learning to explain himself, saying:

sentences.zh: 言未既，有笑於列者曰：「先生欺予哉！

translations.literal: Before the words were finished, someone laughing in the assembly said: 'Sir, you deceive me!
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished speaking, someone in the assembly laughed and said, "Sir, you deceive me!

sentences.zh: 弟子事先生，於茲有年矣。

translations.literal: Your disciple has served you, sir, for years now.
translations.idiomatic: Your disciple has served you, sir, for years now.

sentences.zh: 先生口不絕吟於六藝之文，手不停披於百家之編。

translations.literal: Sir, your mouth never ceases reciting the texts of the Six Arts; your hand never stops unfolding the compilations of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: Sir, your mouth never ceases reciting the texts of the Six Arts, and your hand never stops unfolding the compilations of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 記事者必提其要，纂言者必鉤其玄。

translations.literal: In recording affairs you always seize the essentials; in compiling words you always hook their profundities.
translations.idiomatic: In recording affairs you always seize the essentials; in compiling words you always hook their profundities.

sentences.zh: 貪多務得，細大不捐。

translations.literal: Greedy for much and striving to obtain, you let nothing large or small go.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy for abundance and striving to obtain it, you let nothing large or small go.

sentences.zh: 燒膏油以繼晷，常矻矻以窮年。

translations.literal: You burn lamp oil to extend the sundial's shadow, constantly toiling thus through the year.
translations.idiomatic: You burn lamp oil to extend the sundial's shadow, constantly toiling thus through the year.

sentences.zh: 先生之業，可謂勤矣。

translations.literal: Sir, in your labors, one may say you have been diligent.
translations.idiomatic: Sir, in your labors one may say you have been diligent.

sentences.zh: 牴排異端，攘斥佛、老；

translations.literal: You repel heterodox teachings and drive off Buddhism and Daoism;
translations.idiomatic: You repel heterodox teachings and drive off Buddhism and Daoism;

sentences.zh: 補苴罅漏，張皇幽眇；

translations.literal: you patch leaks and gaps and expand what is hidden and subtle;
translations.idiomatic: you patch leaks and gaps and expand what is hidden and subtle;

sentences.zh: 尋墜緒之茫茫，獨旁搜而遠紹；

translations.literal: you seek fallen threads in vast obscurity, alone searching widely and carrying them far back;
translations.idiomatic: you seek fallen threads in vast obscurity, alone searching widely and carrying them far back;

sentences.zh: 障百川而東之，回狂瀾於既倒。

translations.literal: you block the hundred streams and turn them east, turning back the raging flood already fallen.
translations.idiomatic: you block the hundred streams and turn them east, turning back the raging flood already fallen.

sentences.zh: 先生之於儒，可謂有勞矣。

translations.literal: Sir, in Confucian learning, one may say you have labored.
translations.idiomatic: Sir, in Confucian learning one may say you have labored.

sentences.zh: 沈浸醲郁，含英咀華，作為文章，其書滿家。

translations.literal: Immersed in rich fragrance, savoring blossoms and chewing splendor, you compose writings, and your books fill the house.
translations.idiomatic: Immersed in rich fragrance, savoring blossoms and chewing splendor, you compose writings until your books fill the house.

sentences.zh: 上規姚、姒，渾渾無涯；

translations.literal: Above you take Yao and Si as models, vast and without limit;
translations.idiomatic: Above you take Yao and Si as models, vast and without limit;

sentences.zh: 《周誥》、《殷盤》，佶屈聱牙；

translations.literal: the 'Announcements of Zhou' and 'Pan-geng' of Yin are gnarled, twisted, and hard in the mouth;
translations.idiomatic: the Announcements of Zhou and Pan-geng of Yin are gnarled, twisted, and hard in the mouth;

sentences.zh: 《春秋》謹嚴，《左氏》浮誇；

translations.literal: the Spring and Autumn Annals are strict and careful, the Zuo Tradition is inflated and extravagant;
translations.idiomatic: the Spring and Autumn Annals are strict and careful; the Zuo Tradition is inflated and extravagant;

sentences.zh: 《易》奇而法，《詩》正而葩；

translations.literal: the Changes are marvelous yet patterned, the Odes are upright yet ornate;
translations.idiomatic: the Changes are marvelous yet patterned; the Odes are upright yet ornate;

sentences.zh: 下迨《莊》、《騷》，太史所錄，子雲、相如，同工異曲。

translations.literal: down to Zhuangzi and the Songs of Chu, what the Grand Historian recorded, Yang Yun and Sima Xiangru—same craft, different tunes.
translations.idiomatic: down to Zhuangzi and the Songs of Chu, what the Grand Historian recorded, Yang Yun and Sima Xiangru—same craft, different tunes.

sentences.zh: 先生之於文，可謂閎其中而肆其外矣。

translations.literal: Sir, in literature, one may say you are broad within and free without.
translations.idiomatic: Sir, in literature one may say you are broad within and free without.

sentences.zh: 少始知學，勇於敢為；

translations.literal: In youth you first knew learning and were bold in daring action;
translations.idiomatic: In youth you first knew learning and were bold in daring action;

sentences.zh: 長通於方，左右具宜。

translations.literal: grown, you mastered the ways, fitting all around.
translations.idiomatic: grown, you mastered the ways, fitting all around.

sentences.zh: 先生之於為人，可謂成矣。

translations.literal: Sir, in conduct, one may say you have succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Sir, in conduct one may say you have succeeded.

sentences.zh: 然而公不見信於人，私不見助於友；

translations.literal: Yet publicly you are not trusted by people, privately you are not aided by friends;
translations.idiomatic: Yet publicly you are not trusted by people, and privately you are not aided by friends;

sentences.zh: 跋前躓後，動輒得咎。

translations.literal: stumbling forward and tripping back, at every move you meet blame.
translations.idiomatic: stumbling forward and tripping back, at every move you meet blame.

sentences.zh: 暫為御史，遂竄南夷；

translations.literal: Briefly made censor, then banished to the southern barbarians;
translations.idiomatic: briefly made censor, then banished to the southern barbarians;

sentences.zh: 三為博士，冗不見治。

translations.literal: three times made erudite, superfluous and unseen in governance.
translations.idiomatic: three times made erudite, superfluous and unseen in governance.

sentences.zh: 命與仇謀，取敗幾時。

translations.literal: Fate conspires with enmity; defeat was only a matter of time.
translations.idiomatic: Fate conspires with enmity; defeat was only a matter of time.

sentences.zh: 冬暖而兒號寒，年豐而妻啼饑。

translations.literal: Winter warm yet your children cry with cold; harvest abundant yet your wife weeps with hunger.
translations.idiomatic: Winter is warm yet your children cry with cold; the harvest is abundant yet your wife weeps with hunger.

sentences.zh: 頭童齒豁，竟死何裨？

translations.literal: Head bald and teeth fallen out—what good if you die at last?
translations.idiomatic: Head bald and teeth fallen out—what good if you die at last?

sentences.zh: 不知慮此，而反教人為！」

translations.literal: Not knowing to consider this, yet instead teaching people how to live!'
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing to consider this, yet instead teaching people how to live!"

sentences.zh: 先生曰：「吁，子來前！

translations.literal: The master said: 'Ah, come forward, my son!
translations.idiomatic: The master said, "Ah, come forward, my son!

sentences.zh: 夫大木為杗，細木為桷，欂櫨侏儒，椳闑扂楔，各得其宜，施以成室者，匠氏之工也。

translations.literal: Great timbers become ridgepoles, small timbers become rafters; bracket arms, dwarf pillars, door sockets, door pins, and wedges—each gets its proper place, and applied thus a room is completed: that is the carpenter's craft.
translations.idiomatic: Great timbers become ridgepoles, small timbers become rafters; bracket arms, dwarf pillars, door sockets, door pins, and wedges—each gets its proper place, and applied thus a room is completed: that is the carpenter's craft.

sentences.zh: 玉劄丹砂，赤箭青芝，朱溲馬勃，敗鼓之皮，俱收並蓄，待用無遺者，醫師之良也。

translations.literal: Jade thorn, cinnabar, red arrow, blue lingzhi, red soak, horse dung fungus, and the skin of a broken drum—all are gathered and stored, kept without omission for use: that is the good physician.
translations.idiomatic: Jade thorn, cinnabar, red arrow, blue lingzhi, red soak, horse dung fungus, and the skin of a broken drum—all are gathered and stored, kept without omission for use: that is the good physician.

sentences.zh: 登明選公，雜進巧拙，紆餘為妍，卓犖為傑，校短量長，唯器是適者，宰相之方也。

translations.literal: Ascending to clarity and selecting the worthy, mixing the skillful and the clumsy, turning what is ample into beauty and what is outstanding into excellence, comparing short and measuring long, fitting only the vessel—that is the chancellor's way.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending to clarity and selecting the worthy, mixing the skillful and the clumsy, turning what is ample into beauty and what is outstanding into excellence, comparing short and measuring long, fitting only the vessel—that is the chancellor's way.

sentences.zh: 昔者，孟軻好辯，孔道以明，轍環天下，卒老於行。

translations.literal: In the past Mencius loved debate; the way of Confucius was thereby clarified. His carriage tracks circled the realm, yet in the end he aged on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Mencius loved debate; the way of Confucius was thereby clarified. His carriage tracks circled the realm, yet in the end he aged on the road.

sentences.zh: 茍卿守正，大論是弘，逃讒於楚，廢死蘭陵。

translations.literal: Xunzi upheld the orthodox and greatly expounded the great discourse; fleeing slander in Chu, he died in disuse at Lanling.
translations.idiomatic: Xunzi upheld the orthodox and greatly expounded the great discourse; fleeing slander in Chu, he died in disuse at Lanling.

sentences.zh: 是二儒者，吐辭為經，舉足為法，絕類離倫，優入聖域，其遇於世何如也？

translations.literal: These two Confucians—when they spoke, their words became classics; when they stepped, they became models; surpassing their kind and leaving their peers, excelling into the sage's domain—how were they treated by the world?
translations.idiomatic: These two Confucians—when they spoke, their words became classics; when they stepped, they became models; surpassing their kind and leaving their peers, excelling into the sage's domain—how were they treated by the world?

sentences.zh: 今先生學雖勤，不由其統；

translations.literal: Now, sir, though your learning is diligent, it does not follow its tradition;
translations.idiomatic: Now, sir, though your learning is diligent, it does not follow its tradition;

sentences.zh: 言雖多，不要其中；

translations.literal: though your words are many, they do not hit the center;
translations.idiomatic: though your words are many, they do not hit the center;

sentences.zh: 文雖奇，不濟於用；

translations.literal: though your writing is marvelous, it does not serve use;
translations.idiomatic: though your writing is marvelous, it does not serve use;

sentences.zh: 行雖修，不顯於眾。

translations.literal: though your conduct is cultivated, it does not shine among the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: though your conduct is cultivated, it does not shine among the multitude.

sentences.zh: 猶且月費俸錢，歲靡廩粟，子不知耕，婦不知織，乘馬從徒，安坐而食，踵常塗之促促，窺陳編以盜竊。

translations.literal: Yet month by month you spend salary money, year by year you exhaust granary grain; your son does not know plowing, your wife does not know weaving; riding horses with followers, you sit at ease and eat; treading the common path in haste, you peep at old compilations to steal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet month by month you spend salary money, year by year you exhaust granary grain; your son does not know plowing, your wife does not know weaving; riding horses with followers, you sit at ease and eat; treading the common path in haste, you peep at old compilations to steal.

sentences.zh: 然而聖主不加誅，宰臣不見斥，此非其幸哉！

translations.literal: Yet the sage ruler does not punish you, and the chief minister does not dismiss you—is this not your good fortune!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the sage ruler does not punish you, and the chief minister does not dismiss you—is this not your good fortune!

sentences.zh: 動而得謗，名亦隨之。

translations.literal: Move and you meet slander; fame follows as well.
translations.idiomatic: Move and you meet slander; fame follows as well.

sentences.zh: 投閑置散，乃分之宜。

translations.literal: Cast into idleness and scattered posts—that is the proper allotment of your lot.
translations.idiomatic: Cast into idleness and scattered posts—that is the proper allotment of your lot.

sentences.zh: 若夫商財賄之有無，計班資之崇庳，忘己量之所稱，指前人之瑕疵，是所謂詰匠氏之不以杙為楹，而訾醫師以昌陽引年，欲進其豨苓也。」

translations.literal: As for bargaining over the presence or absence of wealth and bribes, calculating the height or lowness of rank and seniority, forgetting what your measure can bear, and pointing out flaws in predecessors—that is what is called reproaching the carpenter for not making a peg into a pillar, and blaming the physician for using changyang to extend years, wishing to advance one's poria cocos.'
translations.idiomatic: As for bargaining over the presence or absence of wealth and bribes, calculating the height or lowness of rank and seniority, forgetting what your measure can bear, and pointing out flaws in predecessors—that is what is called reproaching the carpenter for not making a peg into a pillar, and blaming the physician for using changyang to extend years, wishing to advance one's poria cocos."

sentences.zh: 執政覽其文而憐之，以其有史才，改比部郎中、史館修撰。

translations.literal: Those in power read his essay and pitied him; because he had talent for history, he was changed to Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: Those in power read his essay and pitied him. Because he had talent for history, he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，轉考功郎中、知制誥，拜中書舍人。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, charged with drafting edicts, and appointed Attendant in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel, charged with drafting edicts, and appointed Attendant in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 俄有不悅愈者，摭其舊事，言愈前左降為江陵掾曹，荊南節度使裴均館之頗厚，均子鍔凡鄙，近者鍔還省父，愈為序餞鍔，仍呼其字。

translations.literal: Soon there were those displeased with Yu who gathered his old affairs, saying that when Yu had earlier been demoted to staff officer of Jiangling, Jingnan military commissioner Pei Jun had entertained him quite generously; Jun's son E was altogether vulgar; recently when E returned to the capital to visit his father, Yu composed a preface to send him off and still called him by his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Soon there were those displeased with Yu who dredged up his old affairs, saying that when Yu had earlier been demoted to staff officer of Jiangling, Jingnan military commissioner Pei Jun had entertained him quite generously. Jun's son E was altogether vulgar. Recently, when E returned to the capital to visit his father, Yu composed a preface to send him off and still called him by his personal name.

sentences.zh: 此論喧於朝列，坐是改太子右庶子。

translations.literal: This discussion clamored in the court ranks; for this he was changed to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: This discussion clamored through the court ranks, and for this he was changed to Right Vice Director of the Crown Prince's Household.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔法門寺有護國真身塔，塔內有釋迦文佛指骨一節，其書本傳法，三十年一開，開則歲豐人泰。

translations.literal: At Famen Temple in Fengxiang there was the True Body Pagoda protecting the state; within the pagoda was one joint of the finger bone of Shakyamuni Buddha. Its script transmitted the dharma; every thirty years it was opened once, and when opened the year was abundant and the people at peace.
translations.idiomatic: At Famen Temple in Fengxiang stood the True Body Pagoda protecting the state. Within the pagoda was one joint of the finger bone of Shakyamuni Buddha. Its scripture transmitted the dharma; every thirty years it was opened once, and when opened the year was abundant and the people at peace.

sentences.zh: 十四年正月，上令中使杜英奇押宮人三十人，持香花赴臨臯驛迎佛骨。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourteenth year, the emperor ordered palace envoy Du Yingqi to escort thirty palace women bearing incense and flowers to welcome the Buddha bone at Lingao Post.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourteenth year, the emperor ordered palace envoy Du Yingqi to escort thirty palace women bearing incense and flowers to welcome the Buddha bone at Lingao Post.

sentences.zh: 自光順門入大內，留禁中三日，乃送諸寺。

translations.literal: From Guangshun Gate they entered the inner palace; it remained in the forbidden precincts three days, then was sent to the temples.
translations.idiomatic: From Guangshun Gate they entered the inner palace. It remained in the forbidden precincts three days, then was sent to the temples.

sentences.zh: 王公士庶，奔走舍施，唯恐在後。

translations.literal: Kings, dukes, scholars, and commoners rushed to give alms, fearing to come last.
translations.idiomatic: Kings, dukes, scholars, and commoners rushed to give alms, fearing to come last.

sentences.zh: 百姓有廢業破產、燒頂灼臂而求供養者。

translations.literal: Among the people were those who abandoned their occupations, ruined their property, burned the crown of the head and scorched the arms to seek to make offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Among the people were those who abandoned their occupations, ruined their property, burned the crowns of their heads, and scorched their arms in order to make offerings.

sentences.zh: 愈素不喜佛，上疏諫曰：

translations.literal: Yu had always disliked Buddhism and submitted a remonstrance memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Yu had always disliked Buddhism and submitted a remonstrance memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 漢明帝時始有佛法，明帝在位，才十八年耳。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming of Han's time Buddhism first appeared; Ming was on the throne only eighteen years.
translations.idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Ming of Han, Buddhism first appeared. Ming was on the throne only eighteen years.

sentences.zh: 其後亂亡相繼，運祚不長。

translations.literal: Afterward disorder and ruin followed in succession, and fortunes did not last long.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward disorder and ruin followed in succession, and fortunes did not last long.

sentences.zh: 宋、齊、梁、陳、元魏已下，事佛漸謹，年代尤促。

translations.literal: From Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, and Northern Wei downward, serving Buddhism grew ever more reverent, yet their dynasties were especially brief.
translations.idiomatic: From Song, Qi, Liang, Chen, and Northern Wei downward, reverence for Buddhism grew ever stricter, yet their dynasties were especially brief.

sentences.zh: 唯梁武帝在位四十八年，前後三度舍身施佛，宗廟之祭，不用牲牢，晝日一食，止於菜果。

translations.literal: Only Emperor Wu of Liang was on the throne forty-eight years; thrice before and after he renounced the body and gave to Buddha; in ancestral temple sacrifices he used no livestock; by day he ate one meal, stopping at vegetables and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Only Emperor Wu of Liang was on the throne forty-eight years. Thrice before and after he renounced the body and gave to Buddha. In ancestral temple sacrifices he used no livestock; by day he ate one meal, stopping at vegetables and fruit.

sentences.zh: 其後竟為侯景所逼，餓死臺城，國亦尋滅。

translations.literal: Afterward he was finally driven by Hou Jing, starved to death at Taicheng, and the state soon perished.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he was finally driven by Hou Jing, starved to death at Taicheng, and the state soon perished.

sentences.zh: 事佛求福，乃更得禍。

translations.literal: Seeking fortune through serving Buddha, one instead obtained calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking fortune through serving Buddha, one instead obtained calamity.

sentences.zh: 由此觀之，佛不足信，亦可知矣。

translations.literal: Viewed thus, Buddha is not to be trusted; this too may be known.
translations.idiomatic: Viewed thus, Buddha is not to be trusted; this too may be known.

sentences.zh: 高祖始受隋禪，則議除之。

translations.literal: When Gaozu first received the abdication from Sui, he then discussed abolishing it.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first received the abdication from Sui, he then discussed abolishing Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 當時群臣識見不遠，不能深究先王之道、古今之宜，推闡聖明，以救斯弊，其事遂止。

translations.literal: At that time the ministers' insight did not reach far; they could not deeply examine the way of former kings and what was fitting between ancient and present, extend and clarify sage illumination, and rescue this abuse; the matter then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the ministers' insight did not reach far. They could not deeply examine the way of former kings and what was fitting between ancient and present, extend and clarify sage illumination, and rescue this abuse. The matter then stopped.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗恨焉！

translations.literal: Your servant has resented this!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant has resented this!

sentences.zh: 伏惟皇帝陛下，神聖英武，數千百年以來未有倫比。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering Your Majesty the Emperor—sacred, heroic, and martial—there has been no equal in several thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considering Your Majesty the Emperor—sacred, heroic, and martial—there has been no equal in several thousand years.

sentences.zh: 即位之初，即不許度人為僧尼、道士，又不許別立寺觀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of your accession you did not permit people to be ordained as monks and nuns or Daoist priests, and you did not permit separate founding of temples and abbeys.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of your accession you did not permit people to be ordained as monks and nuns or Daoist priests, and you did not permit separate founding of temples and abbeys.

sentences.zh: 臣當時以為高祖之誌，必行於陛下之手。

translations.literal: Your servant at that time thought Gaozu's intent would surely be carried out by Your Majesty's hand.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant at that time thought Gaozu's intent would surely be carried out by Your Majesty's hand.

sentences.zh: 今縱未能即行，豈可恣之轉令盛也！

translations.literal: Now, though you cannot immediately carry it out, how can you indulge it and let it grow ever more flourishing!
translations.idiomatic: Now, though you cannot immediately carry it out, how can you indulge it and let it grow ever more flourishing!

sentences.zh: 今聞陛下令群僧迎佛骨於鳳翔，御樓以觀，舁入大內，令諸寺遞迎供養。

translations.literal: Now I hear that Your Majesty has ordered the monks as a group to welcome the Buddha bone from Fengxiang, to view it from the imperial tower, carry it into the inner palace, and order the temples in turn to welcome and make offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear that Your Majesty has ordered the monks as a group to welcome the Buddha bone from Fengxiang, to view it from the imperial tower, carry it into the inner palace, and order the temples in turn to welcome and make offerings.

sentences.zh: 臣雖至愚，必知陛下不惑於佛，作此崇奉以祈福祥也。

translations.literal: Though your servant is extremely foolish, he must know that Your Majesty is not deluded by Buddha and does this reverent service to seek blessing and auspice.
translations.idiomatic: Though your servant is extremely foolish, he must know that Your Majesty is not deluded by Buddha and does this reverent service to seek blessing and auspice.

sentences.zh: 直以年豐人樂，徇人之心，為京都士庶設詭異之觀、戲玩之具耳。

translations.literal: It is simply because the year is abundant and the people joyful, indulging people's hearts, setting up strange spectacles and playful devices for the scholars and commoners of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply because the year is abundant and the people joyful, indulging people's hearts, setting up strange spectacles and playful devices for the scholars and commoners of the capital.

sentences.zh: 安有聖明若此而肯信此等事哉！

translations.literal: How could there be sage illumination such as this yet willing to believe such affairs!
translations.idiomatic: How could there be sage illumination such as this yet willing to believe such affairs!

sentences.zh: 然百姓愚冥，易惑難曉，茍見陛下如此，將謂真心信佛。

translations.literal: Yet the common people are foolish and dark, easily deluded and hard to enlighten; if they see Your Majesty thus, they will say you truly believe in Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the common people are foolish and dark, easily deluded and hard to enlighten. If they see Your Majesty thus, they will say you truly believe in Buddha.

sentences.zh: 皆云天子大聖，猶一心敬信；

translations.literal: All say the Son of Heaven is greatly sage, yet still single-mindedly reveres and believes;
translations.idiomatic: All say the Son of Heaven is greatly sage, yet still single-mindedly reveres and believes;

sentences.zh: 百姓微賤，於佛豈合惜身命。

translations.literal: the people are slight and lowly—how should they not spare body and life for Buddha.
translations.idiomatic: the people are slight and lowly—how should they not spare body and life for Buddha.

sentences.zh: 所以灼頂燔指，百十為群，解衣散錢，自朝至暮。

translations.literal: For this they burn the crown and scorch the fingers, in groups of tens and hundreds, strip off clothes and scatter money, from morning to evening.
translations.idiomatic: For this they burn the crown and scorch the fingers, in groups of tens and hundreds, strip off clothes and scatter money, from morning to evening.

sentences.zh: 轉相仿效，唯恐後時，老幼奔波，棄其生業。

translations.literal: Turning to imitate one another, fearing to come late, old and young rush about and abandon their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Turning to imitate one another, fearing to come late, old and young rush about and abandon their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 若不即加禁遏，更歷諸寺，必有斷臂臠身以為供養者。

translations.literal: If it is not immediately forbidden and stopped, and if it passes through the temples further, there will surely be those who sever arms and slice flesh to make offerings.
translations.idiomatic: If it is not immediately forbidden and stopped, and if it passes through the temples further, there will surely be those who sever arms and slice flesh to make offerings.

sentences.zh: 傷風敗俗，傳笑四方，非細事也。

translations.literal: It wounds custom and ruins morals, making laughter in the four directions—not a small matter.
translations.idiomatic: It wounds custom and ruins morals, making laughter in the four directions—not a small matter.

sentences.zh: 佛本夷狄之人，與中國言語不通，衣服殊制。

translations.literal: Buddha was originally a man of barbarian lands; with China his speech did not communicate and his dress was of a different system.
translations.idiomatic: Buddha was originally a man of barbarian lands. With China his speech did not communicate and his dress was of a different system.

sentences.zh: 口不道先王之法言，身不服先王之法行，不知君臣之義、父子之情。

translations.literal: His mouth did not speak the law-words of former kings; his body did not wear the law-conduct of former kings; he did not know the righteousness between ruler and minister or the affection between father and son.
translations.idiomatic: His mouth did not speak the law-words of former kings; his body did not wear the law-conduct of former kings; he did not know the righteousness between ruler and minister or the affection between father and son.

sentences.zh: 假如其身尚在，奉其國命，來朝京師，陛下容而接之，不過宣政一見，禮賓一設，賜衣一襲，衛而出之於境，不令惑於眾也。

translations.literal: Suppose his body were still alive and he bore his state's command and came to court at the capital: Your Majesty would receive and meet him, but no more than one audience at Xuanzheng, one reception by the Office of Ritual Guests, one gift of a suit of clothes, and guards escorting him out of the border—not permitting him to delude the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Suppose his body were still alive and he bore his state's command and came to court at the capital: Your Majesty would receive and meet him, but no more than one audience at Xuanzheng, one reception by the Office of Ritual Guests, one gift of a suit of clothes, and guards escorting him out of the border—not permitting him to delude the multitude.

sentences.zh: 況其身死已久，枯朽之骨，兇穢之餘，豈宜以入宮禁！

translations.literal: How much the less, when his body has long been dead, this withered rotten bone, the remainder of foul filth—should it enter the palace forbidden precinct!
translations.idiomatic: How much the less, when his body has long been dead, this withered rotten bone, the remainder of foul filth—should it enter the palace forbidden precinct!

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「敬鬼神而遠之。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Revere the spirits and ghosts, yet keep them at a distance.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, "Revere the spirits and ghosts, yet keep them at a distance."

sentences.zh: 古之諸侯，行吊於國，尚令巫祝先以桃茢，祓除不祥，然後進吊。

translations.literal: Ancient feudal lords, when conducting condolence within the state, still ordered shamans and invokers first with peach wands and reed brushes to exorcise inauspiciousness, and then advanced condolence.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient feudal lords, when conducting condolence within the state, still ordered shamans and invokers first with peach wands and reed brushes to exorcise inauspiciousness, and then advanced condolence.

sentences.zh: 今無故取朽穢之物，親臨觀之，巫祝不先，桃茢不用，群臣不言其非，御史不舉其失，臣實恥之。

translations.literal: Now, without reason taking a rotten foul thing and personally viewing it—shamans and invokers not first, peach wands and reed brushes not used, ministers not speaking of its wrong, censors not presenting its fault—your servant is truly shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Now, without reason taking a rotten foul thing and personally viewing it—shamans and invokers not first, peach wands and reed brushes not used, ministers not speaking of its wrong, censors not presenting its fault—your servant is truly shamed.

sentences.zh: 乞以此骨付之水火，永絕根本，斷天下之疑，絕後代之惑。

translations.literal: I beg that this bone be handed to fire and water, forever severing the root, cutting off the realm's doubts and ending later generations' delusion.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that this bone be handed to fire and water, forever severing the root, cutting off the realm's doubts and ending later generations' delusion.

sentences.zh: 使天下之人，知大聖人之所作為，出於尋常萬萬也，豈不盛哉！

translations.literal: Let the realm's people know that the greatly sage one's actions go beyond the ordinary by ten thousand ten thousands—would this not be magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: Let the realm's people know that the greatly sage one's actions go beyond the ordinary by ten thousand ten thousands—would this not be magnificent!

sentences.zh: 豈不快哉！

translations.literal: Would this not be joyful!
translations.idiomatic: Would this not be joyful!

sentences.zh: 佛如有靈，能作禍祟，凡有殃咎，宜加臣身。

translations.literal: If Buddha has spirit and can work calamity and harm, whatever misfortune and blame there is, let it be added to your servant's person.
translations.idiomatic: If Buddha has spirit and can work calamity and harm, whatever misfortune and blame there is, let it be added to your servant's person.

sentences.zh: 上天鑒臨，臣不怨悔。

translations.literal: Heaven looks down and witnesses; your servant will not resent or regret.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven looks down and witnesses; your servant will not resent or regret.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，憲宗怒甚。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, Xianzong was extremely angry.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial was submitted, Xianzong was extremely angry.

sentences.zh: 間一日，出疏以示宰臣，將加極法。

translations.literal: After one day he produced the memorial to show the chief ministers and was about to impose the extreme penalty.
translations.idiomatic: After one day he produced the memorial to show the chief ministers and was about to impose the extreme penalty.

sentences.zh: 裴度、崔群奏曰：「韓愈上忤尊聽，誠宜得罪，然而非內懷忠懇，不避黜責，豈能至此？

translations.literal: Pei Du and Cui Qun submitted: 'Han Yu above offended Your Majesty's hearing and truly ought to be punished; yet if he did not harbor loyal earnestness within and avoid demotion and blame, how could he reach this point?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du and Cui Qun submitted, "Han Yu above offended Your Majesty's hearing and truly ought to be punished; yet if he did not harbor loyal earnestness within and avoid demotion and blame, how could he reach this point?

sentences.zh: 伏乞稍賜寬容，以來諫者。」

translations.literal: I humbly beg slight granted lenience, to draw remonstrators.'
translations.idiomatic: I humbly beg slight granted lenience, to draw remonstrators."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「愈言我奉佛太過，我猶為容之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: 'Yu says I serve Buddhism too much; I still bear with him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Yu says I serve Buddhism too much; I still bear with him.

sentences.zh: 至謂東漢奉佛之後，帝王鹹致夭促，何言之乖刺也？

translations.literal: Yet to say that after Eastern Han served Buddhism, emperors and kings all met early death—how piercing and contrary the words!
translations.idiomatic: Yet to say that after Eastern Han served Buddhism, emperors and kings all met early death—how piercing and contrary the words!

sentences.zh: 愈為人臣，敢爾狂妄，固不可赦！」

translations.literal: Yu as a minister of men dares thus to be arrogant and reckless—he truly cannot be pardoned!'
translations.idiomatic: Yu as a minister of men dares thus to be arrogant and reckless—he truly cannot be pardoned!"

sentences.zh: 於是人情驚惋，乃至國戚諸貴，亦以罪愈太重，因事言之，乃貶為潮州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon popular feeling was startled and grieved; even imperial kin and various nobles, also thinking Yu's punishment too heavy, spoke on the matter; he was then demoted to prefect of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon popular feeling was startled and grieved. Even imperial kin and various nobles, also thinking Yu's punishment too heavy, spoke on the matter. He was then demoted to prefect of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 愈至潮陽，上表曰：

translations.literal: When Yu reached Chaoyang, he submitted a memorial, saying:
translations.idiomatic: When Yu reached Chaoyang, he submitted a memorial, saying:

sentences.zh: 臣受性愚陋，人事多所不通，唯酷好學問文章，未嘗一日暫廢，實為時輩推許。

translations.literal: Your servant received a nature foolish and crude; in human affairs he is much unaccomplished; only he intensely loves learning and literature and has never for one day briefly ceased—truly the contemporaries pushed and approved him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant received a nature foolish and crude; in human affairs he is much unaccomplished. Only he intensely loves learning and literature and has never for one day briefly ceased—truly the contemporaries pushed and approved him.

sentences.zh: 臣於當時之文，亦未有過人者。

translations.literal: Your servant in the literature of his time also had none surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant in the literature of his time also had none surpassing others.

sentences.zh: 至於論述陛下功德，與《詩》、《書》相表裏。

translations.literal: As for discussing and setting forth Your Majesty's merit and virtue, it matches the Odes and Documents inside and out.
translations.idiomatic: As for discussing and setting forth Your Majesty's merit and virtue, it matches the Odes and Documents inside and out.

sentences.zh: 作為歌詩，薦之郊廟，紀太山之封，鏤白玉之牒；

translations.literal: Composing songs and odes, presenting them at the suburban altars, recording the feng and shan of Mount Tai, engraving the white jade tablet;
translations.idiomatic: Composing songs and odes, presenting them at the suburban altars, recording the feng and shan of Mount Tai, engraving the white jade tablet;

sentences.zh: 鋪張對天之宏休，揚厲無前之偉跡；

translations.literal: spreading the great blessing facing Heaven, raising and displaying unprecedented traces of achievement;
translations.idiomatic: spreading the great blessing facing Heaven, raising and displaying unprecedented traces of achievement;

sentences.zh: 編於《詩》、《書》之策而無愧，措於天地之間而無虧。

translations.literal: compiled in the strategies of the Odes and Documents without shame, set between Heaven and Earth without fault.
translations.idiomatic: compiled in the strategies of the Odes and Documents without shame, set between Heaven and Earth without fault.

sentences.zh: 雖使古人復生，臣未肯多讓。

translations.literal: Even if the ancients were reborn, your servant would not willingly yield much.
translations.idiomatic: Even if the ancients were reborn, your servant would not willingly yield much.

sentences.zh: 伏以大唐受命有天下，四海之內，莫不臣妾南北東西，地各萬里。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering that Great Tang received the mandate and possessed the realm, within the four seas none failed to be subject north, south, east, and west; each region ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considering that Great Tang received the mandate and possessed the realm, within the four seas none failed to be subject north, south, east, and west; each region ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 自天寶之後，政治少懈，文致未優，武克不綱。

translations.literal: After the Tianbao era, government was slightly lax, literary polish not yet excellent, martial achievement not disciplined.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tianbao era, government was slightly lax, literary polish not yet excellent, martial achievement not disciplined.

sentences.zh: 孽臣奸隸，外順內悖；

translations.literal: Rebellious ministers and treacherous underlings outwardly compliant yet inwardly rebellious;
translations.idiomatic: Rebellious ministers and treacherous underlings outwardly compliant yet inwardly rebellious;

sentences.zh: 父死子代，以祖以孫。

translations.literal: father dead, son succeeding, by grandfather and by grandson.
translations.idiomatic: father dead, son succeeding, by grandfather and by grandson.

sentences.zh: 如古諸侯，自擅其地，不朝不貢，六七十年。

translations.literal: Like ancient feudal lords, they monopolized their lands, not attending court and not paying tribute, for sixty or seventy years.
translations.idiomatic: Like ancient feudal lords, they monopolized their lands, not attending court and not paying tribute, for sixty or seventy years.

sentences.zh: 四聖傳序，以至陛下，躬親聽斷，干戈所麾，無不從順。

translations.literal: Four sage rulers passed in order down to Your Majesty; personally you hear and decide; where spears and halberds were waved, none failed to follow and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Four sage rulers passed in order down to Your Majesty; personally you hear and decide; where spears and halberds were waved, none failed to follow and submit.

sentences.zh: 宜定樂章，以告神明；

translations.literal: It is fitting to fix music and rites and report to the spirits;
translations.idiomatic: It is fitting to fix music and rites and report to the spirits;

sentences.zh: 東巡泰山，奏功皇天，使永永萬年，服我成烈。

translations.literal: east to tour Mount Tai, present achievement to August Heaven, making forever ten thousand years serve our accomplished merit.
translations.idiomatic: east to tour Mount Tai, present achievement to August Heaven, making forever ten thousand years serve our accomplished merit.

sentences.zh: 當此之際，所謂千載一時，不可逢之嘉會。

translations.literal: At this time, what is called once in a thousand years—an auspicious meeting not to be encountered.
translations.idiomatic: At this time, what is called once in a thousand years—an auspicious meeting not to be encountered.

sentences.zh: 而臣負罪嬰釁，自拘海島，戚戚嗟嗟，日與死迫；

translations.literal: Yet your servant bears guilt and wears offense, self-restrained on a sea island, sorrowful and sighing, day by day pressed by death;
translations.idiomatic: Yet your servant bears guilt and wears offense, self-restrained on a sea island, sorrowful and sighing, day by day pressed by death;

sentences.zh: 曾不得奏薄伎於從官之內、隸御之間，窮思畢精，以贖前過。

translations.literal: never able to present slight skill within attendant officials and among subordinate attendants, exhausting thought and finishing refinement, to redeem former faults.
translations.idiomatic: never able to present slight skill within attendant officials and among subordinate attendants, exhausting thought and finishing refinement, to redeem former faults.

sentences.zh: 懷痛窮天，死不閉目！

translations.literal: Bearing pain reaching Heaven, at death the eyes will not close!
translations.idiomatic: Bearing pain reaching Heaven, at death the eyes will not close!

sentences.zh: 瞻望宸極，魂神飛去。

translations.literal: Gazing toward the imperial pole, soul and spirit fly away.
translations.idiomatic: Gazing toward the imperial pole, soul and spirit fly away.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下，天地父母，哀而憐之。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering Your Majesty, Heaven and Earth's father and mother, pity and cherish him.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considering Your Majesty, Heaven and Earth's father and mother, pity and cherish him.

sentences.zh: 憲宗謂宰臣曰：「昨得韓愈到潮州表，因思其所諫佛骨事，大是愛我，我豈不知！

translations.literal: Xianzong told the chief ministers: 'Yesterday I received Han Yu's memorial arriving at Chaozhou; thinking of his remonstrance on the Buddha bone affair, it greatly loved me—how would I not know!
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong told the chief ministers, "Yesterday I received Han Yu's memorial arriving at Chaozhou. Thinking of his remonstrance on the Buddha bone affair, it greatly loved me—how would I not know!

sentences.zh: 然愈為人臣，不當言人主事佛乃年促也。

translations.literal: Yet Yu as a minister of men ought not to say that when the sovereign serves Buddha his years are brief.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yu as a minister of men ought not to say that when the sovereign serves Buddha his years are brief.

sentences.zh: 我以是惡其容易。」

translations.literal: For this I dislike his rashness.'
translations.idiomatic: For this I dislike his rashness."

sentences.zh: 上欲復用愈，故先語及，觀宰臣之奏對。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to employ Yu again, so he first spoke of it and observed the chief ministers' replies.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to employ Yu again, so he first spoke of it and observed the chief ministers' replies.

sentences.zh: 而皇甫镈惡愈狷直，恐其復用，率先對曰：「愈終大狂疏，且可量移一郡。」

translations.literal: But Huangfu Bo hated Yu's upright bluntness, fearing his reuse, and was first to reply: 'Yu in the end is greatly arrogant and careless; for now he may be transferred in rank to another prefecture.'
translations.idiomatic: But Huangfu Bo hated Yu's upright bluntness, fearing his reuse, and was first to reply, "Yu in the end is greatly arrogant and careless; for now he may be transferred in rank to another prefecture."

sentences.zh: 乃授袁州刺史。

translations.literal: He was then appointed prefect of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，愈至潮陽，既視事，詢吏民疾苦，皆曰：「郡西湫水有鱷魚，卵而化，長數丈，食民畜產將盡，以是民貧。」

translations.literal: At first, when Yu reached Chaoyang and had assumed office, he inquired into officials' and people's hardships; all said: 'West of the prefecture in Jiu Pool there are crocodiles; they hatch from eggs and grow, several zhang long, eating the people's livestock and property nearly to exhaustion; for this the people are poor.'
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Yu reached Chaoyang and had assumed office, he inquired into officials' and people's hardships. All said, "West of the prefecture in Jiu Pool there are crocodiles. They hatch from eggs and grow, several zhang long, eating the people's livestock and property nearly to exhaustion. For this the people are poor."

sentences.zh: 居數日，愈往視之，令判官秦濟砲一豚一羊，投之湫水，祝之曰：

translations.literal: After several days Yu went to view it, ordered aide Qin Ji to fire one pig and one sheep, cast them into Jiu Pool, and prayed, saying:
translations.idiomatic: After several days Yu went to view it, ordered aide Qin Ji to fire one pig and one sheep, cast them into Jiu Pool, and prayed, saying:

sentences.zh: 祝之夕，有暴風雷起於湫中。

translations.literal: On the night of the prayer, violent wind and thunder arose in the pool.
translations.idiomatic: On the night of the prayer, violent wind and thunder arose in the pool.

sentences.zh: 數日，湫水盡涸，徙於舊湫西六十里。

translations.literal: Several days later Jiu Pool completely dried; they moved to sixty li west of the old pool.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later Jiu Pool completely dried; they moved to sixty li west of the old pool.

sentences.zh: 自是潮人無鱷患。

translations.literal: From this the people of Chao had no crocodile trouble.
translations.idiomatic: From this the people of Chao had no crocodile trouble.

sentences.zh: 袁州之俗，男女隸於人者，逾約則沒入出錢之家。

translations.literal: In Yuanzhou's custom, men and women enslaved to others, if they exceeded the contract, were confiscated into the money-lending household.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhou's custom, men and women enslaved to others, if they exceeded the contract, were confiscated into the money-lending household.

sentences.zh: 愈至，設法贖其所沒男女，歸其父母。

translations.literal: When Yu arrived, he set up methods to redeem the confiscated men and women and return them to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu arrived, he set up methods to redeem the confiscated men and women and return them to their parents.

sentences.zh: 仍削其俗法，不許隸人。

translations.literal: He still abolished that local custom, not permitting enslavement of people.
translations.idiomatic: He still abolished that local custom, not permitting enslavement of people.

sentences.zh: 十五年，徵為國子祭酒，轉兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was summoned as Libationer of the Directorate of Education, then transferred to Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was summoned as Libationer of the Directorate of Education, then transferred to Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 會鎮州殺田弘正，立王廷湊，令愈往鎮州宣諭。

translations.literal: It happened that Zhenzhou killed Tian Hongzheng and set up Wang Tingcou; the order made Yu go to Zhenzhou to proclaim and instruct.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Zhenzhou killed Tian Hongzheng and set up Wang Tingcou. The order made Yu go to Zhenzhou to proclaim and instruct.

sentences.zh: 愈既至，集軍民，諭以逆順。

translations.literal: When Yu had arrived, he gathered army and people and instructed them on rebellion and submission.
translations.idiomatic: When Yu had arrived, he gathered army and people and instructed them on rebellion and submission.

sentences.zh: 辭情切至，廷湊畏重之。

translations.literal: His words were earnest to the utmost; Tingcou feared and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: His words were earnest to the utmost; Tingcou feared and honored him.

sentences.zh: 改吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: He was changed to Vice Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 轉京兆尹，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, concurrently Grand Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to metropolitan governor of Jingzhao, concurrently Grand Censor.

sentences.zh: 以不臺參，為御史中丞李紳所劾。

translations.literal: Because he did not attend the censorate assembly, he was impeached by Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Because he did not attend the censorate assembly, he was impeached by Vice Censor-in-Chief Li Shen.

sentences.zh: 愈不伏，言準敕仍不臺參。

translations.literal: Yu did not submit; he said that by edict standard he still did not attend the censorate assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Yu did not submit; he said that by edict standard he still did not attend the censorate assembly.

sentences.zh: 紳、愈性皆褊僻，移刺往來，紛然不止，乃出紳為浙西觀察使，愈亦罷尹為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Shen and Yu were both by nature narrow and eccentric; transfer memorials went back and forth, clamoring without stop; Shen was then sent out as Zhexi observation commissioner, and Yu also was removed as governor and made Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Shen and Yu were both by nature narrow and eccentric. Transfer memorials went back and forth, clamoring without stop. Shen was then sent out as Zhexi observation commissioner, and Yu also was removed as governor and made Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 及紳面辭赴鎮，泣涕陳敘。

translations.literal: When Shen faced farewell to depart to his command, he wept and tearfully stated his case.
translations.idiomatic: When Shen faced farewell to depart to his command, he wept and tearfully stated his case.

sentences.zh: 穆宗憐之，乃追制以紳為兵部侍郎，愈復為吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Muzong pitied him and then issued a follow-up edict making Shen Vice Minister of War; Yu again became Vice Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong pitied him and then issued a follow-up edict making Shen Vice Minister of War. Yu again became Vice Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 十二月卒，時年五十七，贈禮部尚書，謚曰文。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he died, aged fifty-seven; posthumously made Minister of Rites; posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he died, aged fifty-seven. He was posthumously made Minister of Rites with the posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 愈性弘通，與人交，榮悴不易。

translations.literal: Yu's nature was broad and penetrating; in befriending people, glory and decline did not change.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's nature was broad and penetrating. In befriending people, glory and decline did not change.

sentences.zh: 少時與洛陽人孟郊、東郡人張籍友善。

translations.literal: In youth he was friendly with Meng Jiao of Luoyang and Zhang Ji of Dongjun.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was friendly with Meng Jiao of Luoyang and Zhang Ji of Dongjun.

sentences.zh: 二人名位未振，愈不避寒暑，稱薦於公卿間，而籍終成科第，榮於祿仕。

translations.literal: The two men's fame and position were not yet risen; Yu did not avoid cold and heat, praising and recommending them among ministers and grandees; Ji in the end completed the degree and was honored in salary office.
translations.idiomatic: The two men's fame and position were not yet risen. Yu did not avoid cold and heat, praising and recommending them among ministers and grandees. Ji in the end completed the degree and was honored in salary office.

sentences.zh: 後雖通貴，每退公之隙，則相與談宴，論文賦詩，如平昔焉。

translations.literal: Later, though passing to high honor, whenever he retired from public duty's gaps, then together they talked and feasted, discussed literature and composed poetry, as in former days.
translations.idiomatic: Later, though passing to high honor, whenever he retired from public duty's gaps, they together talked and feasted, discussed literature and composed poetry, as in former days.

sentences.zh: 而觀諸權門豪士，如僕隸焉，瞪然不顧。

translations.literal: Yet viewing various powerful gates and heroic gentlemen, like servants and slaves, he stared without regard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet viewing various powerful gates and heroic gentlemen like servants and slaves, he stared without regard.

sentences.zh: 而頗能誘厲後進，館之者十六七，雖晨炊不給，怡然不介意。

translations.literal: Yet he was quite able to entice and encourage later comers; those he lodged were six or seven out of ten; though morning cooking was not supplied, he was pleased and did not mind.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was quite able to entice and encourage later comers. Those he lodged were six or seven out of ten. Though morning cooking was not supplied, he was pleased and did not mind.

sentences.zh: 大抵以興起名教，弘獎仁義為事。

translations.literal: Broadly he took raising the name of teaching and broadly encouraging benevolence and righteousness as his affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Broadly he took raising the name of teaching and broadly encouraging benevolence and righteousness as his affairs.

sentences.zh: 凡嫁內外及友朋孤女僅十人。

translations.literal: In all he married off nearly ten orphaned daughters inside and outside the family and among friends.
translations.idiomatic: In all he married off nearly ten orphaned daughters inside and outside the family and among friends.

sentences.zh: 常以為自魏、晉已還，為文者多拘偶對，而經誥之指歸，遷、雄之氣格，不復振起矣。

translations.literal: He always thought that from Wei and Jin onward, those who wrote literature mostly clung to parallel couplets, while the directives of classics and edicts and the spirit and style of Sima Qian and Yang Xiong no longer revived.
translations.idiomatic: He always thought that from Wei and Jin onward, those who wrote literature mostly clung to parallel couplets, while the directives of classics and edicts and the spirit and style of Sima Qian and Yang Xiong no longer revived.

sentences.zh: 故愈所為，文，務反近體；

translations.literal: Therefore what Yu did in literature strove to reverse recent forms;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore what Yu did in literature strove to reverse recent forms;

sentences.zh: 抒意立言，自成一家新語。

translations.literal: expressing intent and establishing words, he himself became one family's new language.
translations.idiomatic: expressing intent and establishing words, he himself became one family's new language.

sentences.zh: 後學之士，取為師法。

translations.literal: Later-learning scholars took him as teacher and model.
translations.idiomatic: Later-learning scholars took him as teacher and model.

sentences.zh: 當時作者甚眾，無以過之，故世稱「韓文」焉。

translations.literal: Writers of the time were very many; none could surpass him; therefore the age called it 'Han wen.'
translations.idiomatic: Writers of the time were very many; none could surpass him; therefore the age called it "Han wen."

sentences.zh: 然時有恃才肆意，亦有盩孔、孟之旨。

translations.literal: Yet at times relying on talent he acted willfully; there were also points that overturned Confucius and Mencius.
translations.idiomatic: Yet at times relying on talent he acted willfully; there were also points that overturned Confucius and Mencius.

sentences.zh: 若南人妄以柳宗元為羅池神，而愈撰碑以實之；

translations.literal: For example, southerners falsely took Liu Zongyuan as the god of Luo Pool, and Yu composed a stele inscription to substantiate it;
translations.idiomatic: For example, southerners falsely took Liu Zongyuan as the god of Luo Pool, and Yu composed a stele inscription to substantiate it;

sentences.zh: 李賀父名晉，不應進士，而愈為賀作《諱辨》，令舉進士；

translations.literal: Li He's father's name was Jin; he ought not take the jinshi examination, yet Yu composed 'On the Taboo' for He, making him take the jinshi;
translations.idiomatic: Li He's father's name was Jin; he ought not take the jinshi examination, yet Yu composed On the Taboo for He, making him take the jinshi;

sentences.zh: 又為《毛穎傳》，譏戲不近人情：此文章之甚紕繆者。

translations.literal: again he composed 'Biography of Brush Mao,' mocking play not near human feeling: these are the greatest errors in his literature.
translations.idiomatic: again he composed Biography of Brush Mao, mocking play not near human feeling: these are the greatest errors in his literature.

sentences.zh: 時謂愈有史筆，及撰《順宗實錄》，繁簡不當，敘事拙於取舍，頗為當代所非。

translations.literal: The age said Yu had the historian's brush; yet when he compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Shunzong, complexity and simplicity were not fitting, narrating affairs clumsy in choosing and discarding, quite criticized by contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: The age said Yu had the historian's brush; yet when he compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Shunzong, complexity and simplicity were not fitting, narrating affairs clumsy in choosing and discarding, quite criticized by contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 穆宗、文宗嘗詔史臣添改，時愈婿李漢、蔣系在顯位，諸公難之。

translations.literal: Muzong and Wenzong once ordered historiographers to add and revise; at that time Yu's sons-in-law Li Han and Jiang Xi were in prominent position; various lords found it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Muzong and Wenzong once ordered historiographers to add and revise. At that time Yu's sons-in-law Li Han and Jiang Xi were in prominent position; various lords found it difficult.

sentences.zh: 而韋處厚竟別撰《順宗實錄》三卷。

translations.literal: Yet Wei Chuhou finally separately compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Shunzong in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Wei Chuhou finally separately compiled the Veritable Record of Emperor Shunzong in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 有文集四十卷，李漢為之序。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in forty scrolls; Li Han composed the preface for it.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collected works in forty scrolls; Li Han composed the preface for it.

sentences.zh: 子昶，亦登進士第。

translations.literal: His son Chang also passed the jinshi degree.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chang also passed the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 張籍者，貞元中登進士第。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji passed the jinshi degree in the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji passed the jinshi degree in the Zhenyuan era.

sentences.zh: 性詭激，能為古體詩，有警策之句傳於時。

translations.literal: His nature was eccentric and sharp; he could compose ancient-style poetry, with warning and goading lines transmitted in his time.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was eccentric and sharp. He could compose ancient-style poetry, with warning and goading lines transmitted in his time.

sentences.zh: 調補太常寺太祝，轉國子助教、秘書郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred and appointed Grand Invoker of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred to Assistant Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred and appointed Grand Invoker of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then transferred to Assistant Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Secretary.

sentences.zh: 以詩名當代，公卿裴度、令狐楚，才名如白居易、元稹，皆與之遊，而韓愈尤重之。

translations.literal: With poetic fame in his generation, ministers and grandees Pei Du and Linghu Chu, and talents famed like Bai Juyi and Yuan Zhen, all traveled with him; Han Yu especially valued him.
translations.idiomatic: With poetic fame in his generation, ministers and grandees Pei Du and Linghu Chu, and talents famed like Bai Juyi and Yuan Zhen, all traveled with him. Han Yu especially valued him.

sentences.zh: 累授國子博士、水部員外郎，轉水部郎中，卒。

translations.literal: Repeatedly appointed Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, transferred to Director of the Ministry of Works; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly appointed Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Works and died.

sentences.zh: 世謂之張水部云。

translations.literal: The age called him Zhang of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The age called him Zhang of the Ministry of Works.

sentences.zh: 孟郊者，少隱於嵩山，稱處士。

translations.literal: Meng Jiao in youth hid on Mount Song and called himself a retired gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiao in youth hid on Mount Song and called himself a retired gentleman.

sentences.zh: 李翺分司洛中，與之遊。

translations.literal: Li Ao, deputy commissioner at Luoyang, traveled with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ao, deputy commissioner at Luoyang, traveled with him.

sentences.zh: 薦於留守鄭餘慶，辟為賓佐。

translations.literal: He recommended him to the resident guardian Zheng Yuqing, who recruited him as aide.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended him to the resident guardian Zheng Yuqing, who recruited him as aide.

sentences.zh: 性孤僻寡合，韓愈一見以為忘形之契，常稱其字曰東野，與之唱和於文酒之間。

translations.literal: His nature was solitary, eccentric, and hard to join; Han Yu at one meeting took it as a bond forgetting form, often calling him by his personal name Dongye, and with him exchanged verses amid literature and wine.
translations.idiomatic: His nature was solitary, eccentric, and hard to join. Han Yu at one meeting took it as a bond forgetting form, often calling him by his personal name Dongye, and exchanged verses with him amid literature and wine.

sentences.zh: 鄭餘慶鎮興元，又奏為從事，辟書下而卒。

translations.literal: When Zheng Yuqing commanded Xingyuan, he again memorialized him as staff member; the recruitment letter arrived but he died.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Yuqing commanded Xingyuan, he again memorialized him as staff member. The recruitment letter arrived but he died.

sentences.zh: 餘慶給錢數萬葬送，贍給其妻子者累年。

translations.literal: Yuqing gave several tens of thousands in cash for burial and sending, supporting his wife and children for successive years.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing gave several tens of thousands in cash for burial and sending, supporting his wife and children for successive years.

sentences.zh: 唐衢者，應進士，久而不第。

translations.literal: Tang Qu sat for the jinshi examination for a long time without passing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Qu sat for the jinshi examination for a long time without passing.

sentences.zh: 能為歌詩，意多感發。

translations.literal: He could compose songs and poetry; his intent was much moved and aroused.
translations.idiomatic: He could compose songs and poetry; his intent was much moved and aroused.

sentences.zh: 見人文章有所傷嘆者，讀訖必哭，涕泗不能已。

translations.literal: Seeing others' writings with matters that wounded and sighed, after reading he always wept, tears and mucus not stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing others' writings with matters that wounded and sighed, after reading he always wept, tears and mucus not stopping.

sentences.zh: 每與人言論，既相別，發聲一號，音辭哀切，聞之者莫不淒然泣下。

translations.literal: Whenever he discussed with people, after they parted he uttered one cry; his voice and words were mournful and cutting; those who heard were all bleak and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he discussed with people, after they parted he uttered one cry. His voice and words were mournful and cutting; those who heard were all bleak and wept.

sentences.zh: 嘗客遊太原，屬戎帥軍宴，衢得預會。

translations.literal: He once traveled as a guest to Taiyuan; it happened the military commander held an army feast, and Qu was able to join the meeting.
translations.idiomatic: He once traveled as a guest to Taiyuan. It happened the military commander held an army feast, and Qu was able to join the meeting.

sentences.zh: 酒酣言事，抗音而哭，一席不樂，為之罷會，故世稱唐衢善哭。

translations.literal: When wine was deep and he spoke of affairs, he cried with raised voice; the whole seat was not joyful; for this the meeting was dismissed; therefore the age called Tang Qu good at weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When wine was deep and he spoke of affairs, he cried with raised voice. The whole seat was not joyful; for this the meeting was dismissed. Therefore the age called Tang Qu good at weeping.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺白居易遺之詩曰：「賈誼哭時事，阮籍哭路歧。

translations.literal: Left Reminder Bai Juyi sent him a poem, saying: 'Jia Yi wept at current affairs, Ruan Ji wept at crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Left Reminder Bai Juyi sent him a poem, saying, "Jia Yi wept at current affairs, Ruan Ji wept at crossroads.

sentences.zh: 唐生今亦哭，異代同其悲。

translations.literal: Tang Sheng now also weeps; a different age, the same grief.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Sheng now also weeps; a different age, the same grief.

sentences.zh: 唐生者何人？

translations.literal: Who is Tang Sheng?
translations.idiomatic: Who is Tang Sheng?

sentences.zh: 五十寒且饑。

translations.literal: Fifty, cold and also hungry.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty, cold and also hungry.

sentences.zh: 不悲口無食，不悲身無衣。

translations.literal: Not grieving mouth without food, not grieving body without clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Not grieving mouth without food, not grieving body without clothes.

sentences.zh: 所悲忠與義，悲甚則哭之。

translations.literal: What he grieves is loyalty and righteousness; when grief is extreme then he weeps it.
translations.idiomatic: What he grieves is loyalty and righteousness; when grief is extreme then he weeps it.

sentences.zh: 太尉擊賊日，尚書叱盜時。

translations.literal: When the Grand Marshal struck rebels, when the Chief Minister rebuked robbers.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Marshal struck rebels, when the Chief Minister rebuked robbers.

sentences.zh: 大夫死兇寇，諫議謫蠻夷。

translations.literal: When the Grand Counselor died at fierce bandits, when the Remonstrance Official was demoted to barbarian lands.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Counselor died at fierce bandits, when the Remonstrance Official was demoted to barbarian lands.

sentences.zh: 每見如此事，聲發涕輒隨。

translations.literal: Whenever he saw such affairs, voice arose and tears always followed.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw such affairs, voice arose and tears always followed.

sentences.zh: 我亦君之徒，鬱鬱何所為？

translations.literal: I too am your master's follower—gloomy, for what do I act?
translations.idiomatic: I too am your master's follower—gloomy, for what do I act?

sentences.zh: 不能發聲哭，轉作樂府辭。」

translations.literal: Unable to utter voice and weep, I turn instead to composing yuefu lyrics.'
translations.idiomatic: Unable to utter voice and weep, I turn instead to composing yuefu lyrics."

sentences.zh: 其為名流稱重若此。

translations.literal: He was valued by famous currents like this.
translations.idiomatic: He was valued by famous currents like this.

sentences.zh: 竟不登一命而卒。

translations.literal: In the end he did not attain one office and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not attain one office and died.

sentences.zh: 李翺，字習之，涼武昭王之後。

translations.literal: Li Ao, styled Xizhi, was a descendant of Prince Wuzhao of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ao, whose courtesy name was Xizhi, was a descendant of Prince Wuzhao of Liang.

sentences.zh: 父楚金，貝州司法參軍。

translations.literal: His father Chujin was judicial aide of Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Chujin was judicial aide of Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 翺幼勤於儒學，博雅好古，為文尚氣質。

translations.literal: Ao in youth was diligent in Confucian learning, broadly elegant and loving antiquity; in writing he prized spirit and substance.
translations.idiomatic: Ao in youth was diligent in Confucian learning, broadly elegant and loving antiquity. In writing he prized spirit and substance.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，授校書郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi degree and was appointed proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi degree and was appointed proofreader.

sentences.zh: 三遷至京兆府司錄參軍。

translations.literal: Three promotions to Registrar of the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted three times to Registrar of the Jingzhao metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 元和初，轉國子博士、史館修撰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was transferred to Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he was transferred to Erudite of the Directorate of Education and Compiler in the Historiography Institute.

sentences.zh: 十四年，太常丞王涇上疏請去太廟朔望上食，詔百官議。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Court of Imperial Sacrifices Aide Wang Jing submitted a memorial requesting removal of morning and new-moon offerings at the ancestral temple; an edict ordered the hundred officials to discuss.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Court of Imperial Sacrifices Aide Wang Jing submitted a memorial requesting removal of morning and new-moon offerings at the ancestral temple. An edict ordered the hundred officials to discuss.

sentences.zh: 議者以《開元禮》，太廟每歲礿、祠、蒸、嘗、臘，凡五享。

translations.literal: Discussants cited the Kaiyuan Rites: the ancestral temple each year had yu, ci, zheng, chang, and la—five offerings in all.
translations.idiomatic: Discussants cited the Kaiyuan Rites: the ancestral temple each year had yu, ci, zheng, chang, and la—five offerings in all.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，玄宗令尚食每月朔望具常饌，令宮闈令上食於太廟，後遂為常。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao Emperor Xuanzong ordered the Imperial Kitchen each month on new and full moon to prepare regular food, ordering the palace women's office to present food at the ancestral temple; afterward it became constant.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao Emperor Xuanzong ordered the Imperial Kitchen each month on new and full moon to prepare regular food, ordering the palace women's office to present food at the ancestral temple. Afterward it became constant.

sentences.zh: 由是朔望不視朝，比之大祠。

translations.literal: From this on new and full moon he did not hold court audience, compared to great sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: From this on new and full moon he did not hold court audience, compared to great sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 翺奏議曰：

translations.literal: Ao submitted a discussion, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Ao submitted a discussion, saying:

sentences.zh: 伏以太廟之饗，籩豆牲牢，三代之通禮，是貴誠之義也。

translations.literal: Respectfully considering ancestral temple offerings—baskets, beans, livestock, and victims—the common rites of the Three Dynasties, this is the meaning of valuing sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully considering ancestral temple offerings—baskets, beans, livestock, and victims—the common rites of the Three Dynasties, this is the meaning of valuing sincerity.

sentences.zh: 園陵之奠，改用常饌；

translations.literal: Offerings at imperial tombs changed to use regular food;
translations.idiomatic: Offerings at imperial tombs changed to use regular food;

sentences.zh: 秦、漢之權制，乃食味之道也。

translations.literal: Qin and Han expedient institutions—this is the way of food flavors.
translations.idiomatic: Qin and Han expedient institutions—this is the way of food flavors.

sentences.zh: 今朔望上食於太廟，豈非用常褻味而貴多品乎？

translations.literal: Now presenting food on new and full moon at the ancestral temple—is this not using regular daily flavors and valuing many kinds?
translations.idiomatic: Now presenting food on new and full moon at the ancestral temple—is this not using regular daily flavors and valuing many kinds?

sentences.zh: 且非《禮》所謂「至敬不饗味而貴氣臭」之義也。

translations.literal: Moreover it is not the meaning in the Rites of 'supreme reverence does not feast on flavor but values qi and odor.'
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it is not the meaning in the Rites of "supreme reverence does not feast on flavor but values qi and odor."

sentences.zh: 《傳》稱：屈到嗜芰，有疾，召其宗老而屬之曰：「祭我必以芰。」

translations.literal: The Tradition says: Qu Dao loved water chestnuts; having illness, he summoned his clan elders and entrusted them, saying: 'When you sacrifice to me you must use water chestnuts.'
translations.idiomatic: The Tradition says: Qu Dao loved water chestnuts. Having illness, he summoned his clan elders and entrusted them, saying, "When you sacrifice to me you must use water chestnuts."

sentences.zh: 及祭，薦芰，其子違命去芰而用羊，饋籩豆脯醢，君子是之。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice they presented water chestnuts; his son disobeyed the command, removed water chestnuts and used sheep, presenting baskets, beans, dried meat, and pickled meats; gentlemen approved this.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice they presented water chestnuts. His son disobeyed the command, removed water chestnuts and used sheep, presenting baskets, beans, dried meat, and pickled meats. Gentlemen approved this.

sentences.zh: 言事祖考之義，當以禮為重，不以其生存所嗜為獻，蓋明非食味也。

translations.literal: Speaking of serving ancestors and forefathers, one ought to take ritual as weighty, not presenting what they loved while alive—this clearly means it is not eating flavor.
translations.idiomatic: Speaking of serving ancestors and forefathers, one ought to take ritual as weighty, not presenting what they loved while alive—this clearly means it is not eating flavor.

sentences.zh: 然則薦常饌於太廟，無乃與芰為比乎？

translations.literal: Then presenting regular food at the ancestral temple—is it not comparable to water chestnuts?
translations.idiomatic: Then presenting regular food at the ancestral temple—is it not comparable to water chestnuts?

sentences.zh: 且非三代聖王之所行也。

translations.literal: Moreover it is not what the sage kings of the Three Dynasties practiced.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it is not what the sage kings of the Three Dynasties practiced.

sentences.zh: 況祭器不陳俎豆，祭官不命三公，執事者唯宮闈令與宗正卿而已。

translations.literal: Moreover sacrificial vessels do not display meat and beans; sacrificial officers are not ordered by the Three Dukes; those executing affairs are only the palace women's director and the Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover sacrificial vessels do not display meat and beans; sacrificial officers are not ordered by the Three Dukes; those executing affairs are only the palace women's director and the Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 謂之上食也，安得以為祭乎？

translations.literal: Calling it presenting food—how can it be taken as sacrifice?
translations.idiomatic: Calling it presenting food—how can it be taken as sacrifice?

sentences.zh: 且時享於太廟，有司攝事，祝文曰：「孝曾孫皇帝臣某，謹遣太尉臣名，敢昭告於高祖神堯皇帝、祖妣太穆皇后竇氏。
